paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua, son of Rabbi Akiva.

[Pesachim 112a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.112a.9) records seven instructions Rabbi Akiva gave his son Rabbi Yehoshua. In [Shevuot 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shevuot.6a.3), Rabbi Yose says that Rabbi Yehoshua, Rabbi Akiva’s son, asked Rabbi Akiva a question.
And so it is in the [Tosefta, beginning of Negaim](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Negaim.1.1).

[Tosefta Ketubot, chapter 4](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Ketubot.4.7), and [Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Ketubot.5.2.3) relate that Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Akiva married on condition that he would neither feed nor support his wife; rather, she would feed him, support him and teach him Torah (so that he could study Torah). See [the entry on Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha in Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1768&lang=en).

notes.text: The linked Shevuot and Tosefta Negaim have Rabbi Yose recount Yehoshua’s question to his father about how the shades of skin afflictions are counted. Both Ketubot witnesses give Yehoshua’s wife the obligation to feed him, provide for him and teach him Torah.

Hyman’s parenthesis explains that the arrangement enabled Yehoshua to study Torah. [Heilprin’s entry on Rabbi Akiva’s son](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1767&lang=en) also directs readers to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.
